analysis:
This PR is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (Flint section, head lines ~2058-2077) and docs/developer/test.md (lines 844 and 919). No source code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation or authorization paths are touched, so TB-002/TB-009/TB-011 and the T-053/T-054 controls are unaffected.

The documented behavior change is that Flint is paged-only. Automatic backend selection for a verified FlintModel is treated as explicit paged. The crash-loop guard cannot fall back to contiguous. An explicit contiguous selection, the paged kill switch or a capability veto refuses the load. This is fail-closed and narrows the configuration surface. The related KV quantization text says Flint ignores provider-wide defaults and refuses non-native selections. That also fails closed.

T-041 (prefix cache, SSD tier) is the nearest threat. The docs do not change the TTL, HMAC naming, salt scoping, disk budget or kill switch (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE). Nothing here alters the at-rest artifacts.

The test.md change restricts DARKBLOOM_FLINT_BACKEND to unset or paged and adds test suite names. No secrets or endpoints are exposed.

I did not see the implementing Swift code (EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend, the EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve ignore-defaults path, FlintPagedOnlyBackendTests). The claims are therefore unverified against source. This is a doc-accuracy question and not evidence of a security regression. Integration should confirm that the code PR matches the documented fail-closed behavior, particularly that the paged-only veto cannot be bypassed by the crash-loop guard and that the memory-admission gates still apply to paged serving.
